title: Total variation distance as an integral of density excess
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and suppose that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$. Write $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the (real-valued) Radon–Nikodym derivative of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$. Then the total variation distance between $\mu$ and $
u$ equals the excess mass of $\mu$ over $
u$ on the region where $\mu$ locally dominates $
u$:
\[
	frac{1}{2}\,
orm{\mu - 
u}_{\mathrm{TV}}
= \int_{\left\{\,x \in \Omega \;:\;  rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) \ge 1\,ight\}} \left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x) - 1ight)\, d
u.
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are probability measures on a measurable space Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
